issues.legal_issue: An agreement to sell, even when accompanied by payment of the full consideration and delivery of possession, does not transfer proprietary title to immovable property without a registered conveyance deed.

A prospective purchaser who has performed the agreement to sell and lawfully obtained possession acquires possessory rights protected against the transferor under Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act.
A general power of attorney does not confer title to immovable property where no conveyance or other action transferring title is executed under it.
A will confers no present right in property during the testator’s lifetime.
A licensee whose licence has been validly terminated has no subsisting right to remain in possession and may be evicted by the person holding the rightful possessory title.
A person with rightful possessory title following part performance of an agreement to sell is entitled to eviction and mesne profits against a former owner occupying as a licensee.
